subject: physics
question_text: A batsman hits back a ball straight in the direction of the bowler without changing its initial speed of 12 m/s. If the mass of the ball is 0.15 kg, determine the impulse imparted to the ball. (Assume linear motion of the ball.)

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER (numerical). The 1+1 split — formula, then value — is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher. The arithmetic is hand-checked; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula
lines: Impulse = change in momentum. The ball
returns at the same speed, so the
steps.margin_note: The minus sign is the whole question. Take the return velocity as negative.
steps.why: The speed is unchanged but the VELOCITY is not — it reverses. So the change is 2u, not zero, which is why the hit is felt at all.
common_mistakes: Answering zero because the speed did not change.

recall.must_convey: That impulse is the change in momentum and the reversal makes it 2mu.
accept: velocity reverses so it is two m u

steps.memory_tip: Speed is 12 both ways, but the velocity goes from +12 to −12. The change is 24, not 0.

steps.label: The value

lines.text: I = 3.6 N s, towards the bowler

steps.margin_note: Write the unit and the direction. An unlabelled 3.6 is not an impulse.
steps.why: Impulse carries the units of momentum because that is exactly what it is — the momentum handed to the ball during the hit.
common_mistakes: Leaving the unit off, or writing newtons instead of newton-second.

recall.must_convey: That the impulse works out to 3.6 N s.
accept: three point six kg meter per second

steps.memory_tip: Double the mass first: 0.3 × 12 = 3.6 N s. Without the 2 the answer would be 1.8.

insider_note: Both marks rest on one minus sign. An answer of zero, because the speed did not change, earns nothing.
